headline: Semis and Power Names Surge Mid-Session as Geopolitical Anxiety Keeps a Bid Under Defensive Trades
body_html:
Thursday's session is shaping up as a decisive risk-on day, though with sharp distinctions beneath the surface. Advancing issues outnumber decliners by a roughly 2.4-to-1 margin across the 545-name universe — 380 up against 161 down — and the tape's dominant theme is unmistakably power and silicon. Semiconductors lead all sectors with a gain of 3.66%, trailed at a distance by Homebuilders at 1.47% and Materials at 1.05%. Energy, by contrast, is barely breathing, up just 0.05% despite ongoing Middle East tensions that have choked Strait of Hormuz transits to a trickle.

The session's standout mover is Generac, the generator manufacturer, which is surging nearly 20% intraday — the clearest single-stock expression of a market pricing in infrastructure stress and power-reliability risk. Vicor Corporation, a power-module specialist, is adding another 15.5%, and semiconductor names MaxLinear, United Microelectronics, and Arm Holdings are each up between 7.5% and 8.8%, reinforcing the cohesive theme across the group.

On the downside, pressure is concentrated in enterprise software and select healthcare names, with Pegasystems and Salesforce both lower, and Option Care Health shedding roughly 3%. Into the close, watch whether Semiconductors hold their premium and whether Energy can find any footing as Hormuz headlines continue to evolve.

briefs.headline: Generac Vaults Nearly 20% as Power-Security Trade Takes Center Stage
briefs.body: Generac is the session's most dramatic mover, rising close to 20% intraday in what traders are reading as a direct response to escalating concerns over energy-infrastructure reliability. The generator maker's gain towers over the broader Industrials sector, which is itself up a respectable 0.85%. Vicor Corporation's 15%-plus advance in power-module technology underscores the same thematic bid.

briefs.headline: Hormuz Shipping Data Rattles Energy Markets Even as Sector Lags
briefs.body: Only three vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, according to shipping data, a figure that underscores how dramatically the waterway's throughput has contracted amid the Iran conflict. Despite that supply-risk backdrop, the Energy sector is the session's weakest performer, up just 0.05%, suggesting traders may be more focused on demand uncertainty than near-term supply disruption.

briefs.headline: Arm Holdings and MaxLinear Lead Foundry-and-IP Rally
briefs.body: Arm Holdings and MaxLinear are advancing 7.49% and 8.77% respectively Thursday, helping push the Semiconductors sector to a 3.66% gain — the widest margin of outperformance across any group in today's session. United Microelectronics is adding 7.55%, indicating the rally is broad across chip-design, foundry, and IP licensing sub-segments rather than concentrated in a single name.

briefs.headline: Trump Signals Possible Wind-Down of Iran Conflict, Markets Monitoring Closely
briefs.body: President Trump indicated Thursday that the United States may be nearing the end of its military engagement with Iran, a comment that injected a note of caution into otherwise bullish geopolitical positioning. Diplomats and analysts will watch whether any formal ceasefire framework emerges, as continued uncertainty is visibly shaping sector rotation — notably the outperformance of power-infrastructure equities.

briefs.headline: Bank of England Poised to Break from Fed on Rate Policy
briefs.body: The Bank of England is signaling it will resist following the Federal Reserve's rate-hike trajectory despite persistent inflationary pressure, a policy divergence that is drawing attention in global fixed-income markets. The split between major central banks adds a currency and cross-border capital-flow dimension to an already complex macro backdrop heading into Thursday's close.

briefs.headline: Salesforce and Pegasystems Drag on Software Sector Despite Broader Gains
briefs.body: Enterprise software is the one notable pocket of weakness within an otherwise constructive session, with Salesforce down 2.82% and Pegasystems falling 3.15%. The Software sector is still in positive territory overall, gaining 0.75%, but the divergence between large-cap platform names and the broader group signals selective repositioning rather than a wholesale risk-off move within the space.
